# Writing a handoff

## First: scaffold it, don't author it

```bash
pm new handoff <milestone-id>
```

That mints `handoff.md` from the template, with the id and name filled. **Do not create the file
by hand** — you will invent a structure, and the shipped one is better than the one you invent.
The command never clobbers an existing handoff.

It is deliberately **not** created when a milestone is scaffolded. An absent `handoff.md` is a
signal, and `check pm` warns on it once the milestone is `in_progress` — which is when someone
might actually need to pick the work up. Auto-minting would put an unwritten template in every
milestone and destroy the signal.

If the file exists but opens without its instruction line, `pm new milestone <id>` restores it.
`check grain-shape` is what tells you.

## The one rule

> **A document carries only what nothing else holds. Everything derivable is a command it names.**
> If the handoff and the tree disagree, the tree is right — the tree is maintained by gates, the
> handoff by whoever remembered.

So before writing any line, ask: **does a command already answer this?** If yes, name the command.

| do not write | name this instead |
|---|---|
| the feature list, states, story counts | `pm status <id>` |
| what has happened and why | `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD` — the messages carry the arguments |
| what things cost, what was spent | `pm ledger report` |
| the dependency graph | `grep -h '^depends_on' <roadmap>/features/*.md` |
| which gate to run, and how long it takes | `make help`, `verify --plan` |
| decisions and their rejected alternatives | `decisions.md` — point at it, never summarise it |
| whether the tree is self-consistent | `pm validate` |

## What actually belongs

The template's three sections, and the third is the reason the file exists.

**1. Where the work lives.** Branch, version, and the **absolute path** of the checkout. A branch
name is not a location when worktrees are in play, and no command prints where you were supposed
to be. Say who else is working nearby.

**2. Where to pick up.** The next action and what unblocks after it. Delete any command in the
template's block that does not apply here; add none that a command already answers.

**3. Traps this milestone has already sprung.** *Every one of these was paid for.* What looked
true, what was actually true, how it surfaced. **Sections 1 and 2 point at things; this section is
the only part no command can regenerate.** If you are short of time, write this one.

Also belongs, because nothing derives it: a gate whose real cost differs from its recorded median
(a cold cache, a slow machine), a constraint about which files two grains share, and any hazard in
the environment rather than the tree.

## How you know you got it wrong

`check grain-shape` caps a handoff's body. **A handoff that hits its cap is almost always
restating the tree** — that is what the cap is for. Do not raise it; find the paragraph that a
command already answers and replace it with the command.
